history.dynasty: Cholas (present temple built by Rajaraja Chola I); Pandyas (sanctum, ardha mandapa, goddess shrine); Nayaks (Parasakthi shrine, walls, mandapas); Travancore (contributions per Wikipedia)
history.period: Present structure 11th century (Rajaraja Chola I, per Light Up Temples); sanctum additions by Pandyas and Nayaks; glorified in the 7th-century Tevaram
history.summary: CSV CORRECTIONS: (1) Town is NOT Tirunelveli - the temple is in Kutralam (Courtallam), the waterfalls town ~5-6 km west of Tenkasi. (2) District is Tenkasi, not Tirunelveli (Tenkasi became a separate district in 2019; older addresses still say Tirunelveli district). Documented with the corrected location. The CSV name 'Kurumpalaveesar' is the Tamil 'Kurumbala Eesar' - the lord of the Kurumpala (jack tree), the temple's sthala vriksham: the Templenet Encyclopedia lists the deities as 'Kutralanathar - Kurumbala Eesar (Shiva)', and india9.com names the shrine the 'Kurumpalanathar Temple' at Kuttalam. There is no separate 'Kurumpalaveesar Temple' - the CSV row refers to this one shrine. The Kutralanathar Temple is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams (hymns by Sambandar, Appar, Manickavasagar; the 257th Paadal Petra Shiva Sthalam and 13th in Pandya Nadu per one source) and one of the five Pancha Sabhas of Nataraja - the Chitra Sabha, with celebrated murals. Legend says the site was originally a Vishnu temple; Sage Agastya, sent south to balance the earth at Shiva-Parvati's celestial wedding, converted the Vishnu image into a swayambhu lingam and transformed Sridevi and Bhudevi into Kuzhalvaimozhi Nayaki and Parasakthi (the furious Parasakthi being appeased by the Kamakoteeswara Linga before her Dharani Peetam). Local legend also credits Indra with building the temple as atonement, and the Pandavas' visit during exile. Rajaraja Chola I built the present temple and the inner-corridor wall; the Pandyas built the sanctum, ardha mandapa, the goddess's separate sanctum and the Pillayan Kattalai mandapa; the Nayaks built the Parasakthi shrine, periphery wall and streets. Theertham: Shiva Madhu Ganga (North Falls). The conch-shaped temple sits on 3.5 acres amid the Western Ghats' Thirukoodamalai hills, with the falls audible inside the temple.

name: Kutrallam Kurumpalaveesar Temple
town: Kutralam (Courtallam) (CSV town 'Tirunelveli' is WRONG - the temple is in Kutralam, ~5-6 km from Tenkasi; ~58 km from Tirunelveli city)
town_description: Kutralam (Courtallam) is a resort town in the Western Ghats foothills of southern Tamil Nadu, famed as the 'Spa of South India' for its nine waterfalls (Main Falls, Five Falls, Old Courtallam, Shenbaga Devi, Honey Falls and others) whose waters are believed to carry medicinal plant essences. The falls season runs June to September; the Kutralanathar Temple near the Main Falls is the town's oldest landmark.

travel.railway: Tenkasi Junction - about 5-6 km (verify); autos available.
travel.road: In Kutralam town on the Main Falls road; well connected by road from Tenkasi and Tirunelveli (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: June to September (falls season); Maha Shivaratri in February-March is the biggest festival crowd.
